newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurostocks steady despite big rise in US jobs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurostocks steady despite big rise in US jobs.

text.p: The immediate reaction of European bourses to a bigger than expected rise in U.S.employment on Friday was to claw back earlier modest losses and nudge higher.

The U.S. Labor Department reported non-farm payrolls rose by 339,000 in February against a downwardly revised 247,000 increase in January. Economists in a Reuters survey had expected non-farm payrolls to post a 230,000-job gain in February.

"The numbers were unambigously strong, (but the report is)... not going to prompt a March move (to tighten U.S. interest rates)," Wayne Ayers, Chief Economist, Bank of Boston told Financial Television.

Share traders on both sides of the Atlantic fear that a move by the U.S. Federal Reserve central bank to rise interest rates to choke off the threat of inflation could sorely test the global bull market in shares which has seen prices surge to record after record recently

"This report does not change things dramatically in terms of Fed policy. The main strength was in construction, which the Labor Department tied to mild weather. The hourly earnings data, (up three cents to $12.09 in February) didn't cause much of a scare," David Sloan, Senior Economist at I.D.E.A. INC said.

However, Hildegard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities said, - "This is very strong data, way above expectations and bonds are down sharply. It's tellings us that there is a possibility the Fed may raise rates at the next meeting on March 25. Looking at the bonds and the futures I'd have to say we will have a bad day."

At 1400 gmt, London's FTSE index was up 6.2 points at 4405.5, while in Paris the CAC-40 index turned a 15 point loss into a nine point rise and Germany's DAX Ibis index of post-bourse trading was showing a gain of 11.76 points.
Higher interest rates would be bad news for share prices by making the cost of borrowing more expensive for companies and alternative investments more attractive to investors.
Any selloff in U.S. share prices, which are at record levels, would undermine European share prices, too.

Earlier, London's FTSE 100 index crept into record territory at the start but share prices were mixed throughout the morning and dealers said nervousness ahead of the U.S. jobs figures had restrained the market.
But declining stocks outnumbered gainers and dealers said the market's marginal advance was led by a handful of shares, with Glaxo Wellcome, BTR and GKN in the vanguard.

Positive newspaper comment about a bundle of blue-chip annual results released on Thursday, particularly those of Glaxo, helped to stem the downward pressure, traders said. The continued liquidity of the market is also seen helping support shares.
"All the institutions still seem to be awash with cash and obviously that will be a positive factor," one dealer said.
But he added that the market's rise to record heights might prompt some nervousness and profit-taking, saying: "Some people seem to feel slightly giddy up here."
In Paris, profit-taking took French shares lower at the opening after sharp gains in the last few days and Thursday's 1.23 percent rise. Prices rallied a touch, then fell back again towards midday.

The market was well supported, however, with non-resident investors still finding Paris attractive. "They are forced to come in, the market is going up," said one trader. Company earnings were considered good, particularly those of Promodes.
Germany's 30-share blue-chip DAX index began bourse trading sharply lower with traders in Frankfurt seeking inspiration to give direction and cure a hangover from the record run of recent days.
The DAX fell below the 3,400-point level early on and closed -- before the U.S. jobs figures -- at 3,376.2 points, down 41.40 or 1.21 percent.
The dollar was firmer against the mark after the jobs figures and stood at 1.7190 at 1400 gmt, having been around 1.7150 at midday.
Economists had expected a strong rise in payrolls because February is traditionally a month where the figures come in above expectations.
The figures could "...see the dollar make new highs above 1.7230 and maybe even 1.73," Lee Ferridge, foreign exchange strategist at Commerzbank in London said during the morning.
Dollar/yen was looked rather lacklustre in early trade but perked up after the jobs figures and moved towards the higher end of a 121 yen range.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.7190 marks and 121.50 yen, compared with 1.7168 and 121.20 late on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 6.2 points at 4,405.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 2.80 points at 2,701.72.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 41.40 points at 3,376.20.
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1400 GMT
Gold was fixed at $351.70 compared with London's close on Thursday of $352.20.
